title: P0 APPEND-ONLY MEMORY NOT ENFORCED ON FRESH INSTALLS — migration 017 triggers silently dropped by filterForSQLite. detail: Reproduced twice on fresh build at 8e3e7e6, 2026-09-09. Starting the server the README env-var way (CONSENSUS_DB_URL=sqlite:///... CONSENSUS_PORT=8124 ./consensus serve, no config file): the FIRST goal-driven session wedges the entire server. Sequence: 'harness: found active session' -> 'planning: starting interactive session' -> exactly 3m later 'harness: planning failed ... error="planning: initial context: read context: begin tx: sqlite: begin tx: context deadline exceeded"' -> heartbeat auto-retries the same session forever. During the wedged window the API first returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED to the valid admin key, then stops answering entirely (no-auth /api/v1/health times out, HTTP 000). kill -9 -> integrity ok -> restart -> heartbeat resumes the poisoned session -> re-wedges within seconds: a session wedged this way bricks the instance on every boot (only fix is deleting the session/DB). A/B PROOF it is the pool: identical run with config-file database: { max_open_conns: 4 } executes the full loop cleanly (llm: calling provider -> response received -> commands staged -> committing -> idle). The env-var path exposes no max_open_conns override and the WAL grew to 1.5MB on a near-idle DB = pool starvation signature. Fix direction: (1) pin a safe default sqlite pool (max_open_conns<=4 or equivalent) instead of unlimited; (2) put harness transactions on a separate pool/connection class from API reads; (3) stop heartbeat-resume on a session that failed N consecutive planning windows (poison-pill guard); (4) fail loud: 'begin tx deadline' should surface as a 5xx/health-degraded event, not a silent server freeze. Evidence: /tmp/dogfood-consensus/server.log + server2.log (wedged) vs server3.log (clean), same binary.

The unit test internal/api/openapi_paths_test.go:65-69 mounts BOTH '/mcp/*' AND '/mcp' — a mount shape production does not replicate — so all tests pass while the documented mount 404s live (green-tests-riding-a-different-wiring). [dogfood:P0] MCP send_message on a 'booting' session is a SILENT dead letter: tool returns '{"sent": true}' but the session never wakes (stuck booting, iteration 0, tokens 0, zero billing for 5+ min). A/B-proven 2026-09-25: MCP-created session + MCP send_message -> no LLM call ever; the SAME session woke instantly when one message arrived via REST; MCP send on an IDLE session works fine (turn-2 answered). Root cause: internal/mcp/tools.go:287 wakes only 'idle || paused' while the REST path internal/api/service.go:433 wakes 'idle || booting' — sessions are born 'booting', so the MCP path skips the wake for every fresh session. The MCP tool ALSO bypasses MessageService.SendMessage entirely (hand-rolled INSERT with iteration_created=0 and no event publish), so the two write paths drift independently. FIX: make toolSendMessage delegate to MessageService.SendMessage (single write path) or add 'booting' to its wake condition. ACCEPTANCE: MCP create_session -> MCP send_message -> reply appears with no REST call.

detail: PASS CRITERIA: (1) per-turn reasoning_content is persisted alongside the turn (not discarded); (2) when the request carries tools, all previous turns' reasoning_content is re-sent, and when it does not, it is omitted (the provider ignores it and concatenating it is not what the contract says); (3) a test asserts both branches, driven by the presence of tools, using a recorded fixture; (4) thinking-mode control is explicit — the toggle and effort are settable per request rather than inherited silently from the provider default; (5) the current fallback ('reasoning_content as primary output when content == ""') is re-examined: CoT is evidence of thinking, not the answer, and promoting it to content should be a deliberate, logged, last-resort behaviour rather than a silent substitution. CONTRACT: specs/024-shim-support-matrix.md. PROVIDER SOURCES: api-docs.deepseek.com guides/anthropic_api, guides/thinking_mode, guides/tool_calls, guides/chat_prefix_completion. UPSTREAM SOURCE: sst/opencode packages/sdk/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1.1, the single source of truth for server + SDK generation); opencode.ai/docs/server.
reasoning: WHY (measured, file:line): internal/llm/openai_client.go:92 declares ReasoningContent on the request message struct, but the ONLY consumer is line 278 — buildResponse falls back to it when content is empty, logging 'llm: using reasoning_content as primary output (thinking model)'. Nothing stores a turn's CoT and nothing re-sends it. DeepSeek's documented rule is that with tools present, every previous turn's reasoning_content MUST be passed back and is concatenated into context; without tools it must not be. So the moment provider-native tools go on the wire (SHIM-SUPPORT-001), CoT continuity breaks by construction and degrades SILENTLY rather than failing loudly — the model simply loses its earlier reasoning. Secondary: the provider ignores temperature/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty in thinking mode (accepted, no error, no effect) and clamps top_p to >=0.95 in thinking mode / fixes it at 1.0 otherwise, so any harness that believes it is tuning those knobs on DeepSeek is wrong without an error to tell it so.

detail: Repro (dev box, HEAD 4e92fdc3, /tmp/corrupt-test): ./consensus serve --config /nonexistent-abc.yaml starts the server (migrations applied, heartbeat loop started, rc only ends via timeout) — no error, no usage, exit never happens. Root cause: internal/config/config.go LoadWithPath treats os.IsNotExist on ANY resolved path (including the explicit SetConfigPath override wired from --config at internal/cli/serve.go:49) as 'proceed with defaults + env' (config.go:257-263). The silent-fallback contract is correct for auto-discovery (resolveConfigPath only returns paths that exist, config.go:330-337) but an operator-supplied explicit path that does not exist is silently ignored — this is exactly the missing-config behavior the QA battery's chaos-errorpath cell has now failed to pin in two consecutive cycles (QA-CONSENSUS-10, QA-CONSENSUS-17). No spec/doc text pins either behavior (specs/016-cli-interface.md §4/§8 silent on it; docs/DEBUGGING.md lists override paths without a missing-file contract), so the cell cannot grade it. Fix: when configPathOverride is explicitly set and the file is missing, return a config error (exit 1) instead of falling through to defaults; add a chaos-errorpath cell assertion once the contract is pinned. Verified live: rc=124 (timeout) with server fully booted on a nonexistent --config; battery cell chaos-errorpath INFO/UNVERIFIED with the same WARN-then-boot shape on bunker-mvp agent 49709d41.

detail: MEASURED 2026-09-30 against pin 7945de208964a49300d7f770d1a71d078db9a4c4 (v1.18.33); pinned upstream suites = 34 ran / 32 pass / 2 fail. EXACT ASSERTION (packages/opencode/test/server/sdk-error-shape.test.ts, test 'v2 SDK error shape > 404 with NamedError body throws a real Error carrying the server message', test line 30, assertion line 44): expect(err.message).toContain("Session not found"); the same test continues at line 45 with expect(cause.status).toBe(404) and lines 46-49 with expect(cause.body).toMatchObject({name: "NotFoundError", data: {message: expect.stringContaining("Session not found")}}). FAILURE LOG EXCERPT (docs/evidence/opencode-upstream-v1.18.33/packages_opencode_test_server_sdk-error-shape_test_ts.log): 'error: expect(received).toContain(expected)' / 'Expected to contain: "Session not found"' / 'Received: "GET http://test/session/ses_no_such?directory=%2Ftmp%2Fopencode-test-684l17w2e1q -> 404 Not Found"' / '(fail) v2 SDK error shape > 404 with NamedError body throws a real Error carrying the server message [355.24ms]'. LIVE PROBE on the same revision (scratch shim, build from this tree): GET /session/ses_no_such?directory=%2Ftmp -> HTTP 404 with body {"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND","message":"session not found"}}. The STATUS is now correct (at evidence r4 this assertion observed '401 Unauthorized', so the route/auth half has since been fixed); the defect is the BODY ENVELOPE. Upstream's SDK wrapClientError lifts data.message into Error.message only for the NamedError shape {name, data:{message}}, so with the shim's own {error:{code,message}} envelope err.message falls back to the generic fetch text and cause.body misses the shape. FIX DIRECTION: the shim already owns an upstream-shaped typed-not-found helper - writeOpencodeNotFoundError, internal/shim/opencode/server.go:1277, used for ProjectNotFoundError (internal/shim/opencode/server.go:1273) - route session.get's 404 through the upstream NamedError envelope instead of the generic /api envelope. EVIDENCE PATH: docs/evidence/opencode-upstream-v1.18.33/ (summary.md, results.tsv row 3, packages_opencode_test_server_sdk-error-shape_test_ts.log). WHY NO EXISTING ROW COVERED IT: specs/openapi/upstream/opencode-declared-vs-served-1.18.33.json lists session.get (GET /session/{sessionID}, declared 200,400,404) among 'covered' with served_outcome 200 - that comparison models path/method/status, never error-body shape, so this divergence is invisible to it and survived every prior sweep. NOT DUPLICATED: the other failing assertion in the same suite (400-class validation answered as 404 on POST /sync/history/list, SHIM-DRIFT-126) is already tracked by DF-CONSENSUS-40 and SHIM-GAP-004/SHIM-GAP-007 - see those rows rather than this one.
reasoning: WHY: this is the last thing standing between an upstream SDK client and a usable error path. The TUI catches the thrown Error and prints its .message, so a missing session currently surfaces as 'GET http://test/session/... -> 404 Not Found' instead of 'Session not found' - the exact user-facing failure the upstream test was written to prevent. It is also invisible to our own declared-vs-served grader because that grader compares routes, not response bodies, which is why it has survived every sweep to date.

detail: Full battery on JIT agent 69ba129c@dedi-2 (dedi-2 host TZ=Europe/Berlin, UTC+2) at HEAD d0c2d42: go test ./... red in internal/tools — TestCheckToolRateLimit_Exceeded (rate_limiter_test.go:113 'expected rate limit error, got nil') and TestCheckToolRateLimit_SessionIsolation (rate_limiter_test.go:174), 33 other packages ok. Root cause reproduced locally at the same HEAD: rate_limiter_test.go inserts tool_requests with SQLite datetime('now') (always UTC) but CheckToolRateLimit (internal/tools/rate_limiter.go:61) compares created_at >= $3 with since=time.Now().Add(-1*time.Minute) evaluated in the process's LOCAL timezone — under any positive-UTC-offset TZ the driver renders 'now' behind UTC, the 1-minute window misses all fresh rows, recentCount=0, limiter returns nil. Repro (deterministic, not flaky): TZ=Europe/Berlin go test ./internal/tools/ -run TestCheckToolRateLimit -count=1 → FAIL both tests; TZ=UTC and TZ=America/New_York → ok. Evidence: /tmp/qa-consensus-1001/, agent logs qa-logs-369909 (native.log, ci.log). Fix shape: write created_at from Go (time.Now().UTC()) in the test/fixtures and/or normalize the comparison window to UTC on both sides; also audit the SQL-level enforce_tool_rate_limit trigger (migration 001) for the same UTC-vs-local window assumption.

Reproduced: default launch rc=1 on bunker-mvp AND dedi-2 (same 2223 probe); BUNKER_QA_SSH_PORT=22 launch succeeds first try. Harness-side ssh(1) to port 22 works (verified directly). (2) BATTERY TRUNCATION: with the corrected port the battery ran, graded fresh-install OK (go build ./... rc=0 on the clean agent), 7x toolchain-bootstrap OK, then ci-pass FAIL and upgrade N/A — and the qa-run.sh process DIED with no docker-deploy, ui-probe or chaos cell ever attempted (agent-side qa-evidence.jsonl frozen at 10 lines, ts 19:59:38Z, no qa-run process alive afterward). Root causes visible in the artifacts: the agent's per-agent docker socket /run/bunker/a57f586d/docker.sock NEVER appeared (the launch-time Docker Tunnel needs port 2223-equivalent host plumbing that was never established, and qa-run.sh waits only 20x2s then proceeds), so every act job failed 'failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///run/bunker/a57f586d/docker.sock' (ci.log) and the native test leg died 'go: creating work dir: mkdir /tmp/go-build3797955013: no such file or directory' — the shared host /tmp raced with 3+ concurrent qa-run.sh processes from sibling agents (bunker-0d551a16, bunker-af1a0508 both alive on the same host during this run). The battery then exited without grading the remaining cells in any state — a truncated battery must grade every never-run cell SKIPPED/UNVERIFIED before exiting, in all exit paths. PRODUCT EVIDENCE FROM THIS RUN (real, clean-machine): go vet ./... rc=0 and FULL go test ./... -count=1 rc=0 — 37 packages ok, 0 FAIL, [no test files] only for root/chronicle/specs (re-run executed on the same agent after the /tmp race cleared; /tmp/native-rerun.log on the agent). FIX SHAPE: (a) default BUNKER_QA_SSH_PORT must match the per-server reality (server-keyed config, not a global 2223), (b) qa-run.sh must FAIL CLOSED (grade remaining cells SKIPPED + nonzero rc) instead of dying silently when the docker socket never appears or a leg kills the script, (c) serialize /tmp usage per-agent (TMPDIR=$HOME/tmp inside the agent) so concurrent sibling batteries cannot corrupt go-build dirs. A test must cover the MOUNT (an httptest against the chi router built in cmd/consensus/main.go, not the inner web mux), since the existing internal/web tests pass against the inner mux alone and cannot see this.
detail: Reproduced this cycle on the dev box at HEAD 93c3583 from the freshly built binary (`go build -o bin/consensus ./cmd/consensus/`), serve with a sandboxed HOME, a scratch sqlite DB and scratch port 18097. Probe results (raw): GET /ui/ -> 200 text/html; GET /ui/dashboard -> 404 text/plain; GET /ui/sessions -> 404 text/plain; GET /ui/memory -> 404 text/plain; GET /ui/health -> 404 text/plain; GET /dashboard -> 404 text/plain; GET /sessions -> 404 text/plain; GET /memory -> 404 text/plain; GET /ui -> 404. Contrast on the same process: GET /chronicle/ -> 200 text/html, GET /api/v1/health -> 200 application/json. The HTML the server itself emits at /ui/ carries root-absolute nav links — href="/dashboard", href="/sessions", href="/memory" — so the UI's own navigation leaves the /ui prefix. ROOT CAUSE 1 (mount pattern): cmd/consensus/main.go:413 takes the API router as a chi.Router (`apiMux := apiSrv.Handler().(chi.Router)`) and line 424 mounts the admin UI as `apiMux.Handle("/ui/", http.StripPrefix("/ui", webUI.Handler()))` — the only embedded UI mount WITHOUT the `/*` wildcard (cf. `/mcp/*` line 414, `/webhooks/*` line 419, `/chronicle/*` line 429). chi's Handle("/ui/") matches ONLY the exact path "/ui/"; subpaths fall through to chi's NotFound. Mechanism proven with a minimal chi v5.3.1 program (same version as go.mod) mounting an inner mux the same way: pattern "/ui/" -> /ui/dashboard = 404 '404 page not found'; pattern "/ui/*" -> /ui/dashboard = 200 inner-dashboard. ROOT CAUSE 2 (prefix-unaware links): internal/web/server.go emits absolute hrefs (/dashboard, /sessions, /memory, /health) in the pages it serves, and the mux is mounted under a strip-prefix, so even once the wildcard is fixed a click on Dashboard navigates to the origin root /dashboard (observed 404, no such route on the API router) instead of /ui/dashboard. Both must change for the documented UI to work. No test covers the mount: `grep -rn '"/ui' --include=*_test.go internal cmd pkg` is empty, and the web server's own tests exercise the INNER mux directly at /dashboard, which is why CI stays green. RELATED HARNESS OBSERVATION (not this row's defect): the clean-machine battery's ui-probe cell graded "N/A no web UI detected" at 13:02:48Z while /ui/ + /chronicle/ are embedded Go UIs served by `serve` — the detector misses the entrypoint, so this surface is graded by hand this cycle instead of by the battery. Evidence: /tmp/qa-consensus-uiprobe/ui-mount-evidence.txt and /tmp/qa-consensus-uiprobe/serve2.log.

ROOT CAUSE (exact): bunker-qa.sh (233894 B, sha256 b2a9e1178e57e8b749e16c970f4a47d67fbec35d45b76a922876918b31d44085, commit 01c753f4f) builds UI_PORTS in the ui-probe arm as the hardcoded list '3000 5173 8000 8080 8081 8766 8767 9000 9090' PLUS ports scraped from docs: for README.md docs/reference/flags.md docs/flags.md docs/reference/cli.md it runs grep -oE '(--listen|--port|--addr|listen|port)[= :]+[^,;"]*' then grep -oE '[0-9]{4,5}'. On this repo only README.md exists, and that two-stage grep extracts exactly ONE number: 8095 — from the README's 'Port 8090 already in use? (stale sidecar shadowing)' workaround block (README.md:287 'CONSENSUS_PORT=8095 ./bin/consensus serve', :289 './bin/consensus serve --port 8095'). The documented DEFAULT port 8090 is never matched: it appears in README only as 'localhost:8090' / '-p 8090:8090' / '"8090"' / a 'CONSENSUS_PORT | 8090' table row, none of which satisfy the ERE — and 8090 is not in the hardcoded list either. So the probe list contains the WORKAROUND port instead of the default one.
WHY THAT PRODUCES A FALSE VERDICT: the arm starts the server and assigns UI_LISTEN to the first free port in UI_PORTS that answers. The started 'consensus serve' binds 127.0.0.1:8090 (api) AND 127.0.0.1:8095 (pprof debug listener — internal/config/config.go:165 default '127.0.0.1:8095'), both visible in the same ui-probe.log. 8090 is not in the probe list, 8095 is, so the cell sweeps /chat /docs / /ui /dashboard /app /index.html against the PPORF mux, which only serves /debug/pprof/* and answers net/http's default 404 for everything else — hence seven 404 text/plain answers and an INFO 'no HTML surface' verdict.
LIVE PROOF THE PRODUCT DOES SERVE HTML AT THE TESTED HEAD (dev box, binary built from 60e0057, scratch HOME/DB, port 18797): GET /ui/ -> 200 text/html; /ui/dashboard -> 200 text/html; /ui/sessions -> 200; /ui/memory -> 200; /ui/health -> 200; /ui -> 301; index hrefs served at /ui/ are relative (dashboard, memory, sessions) with 0 root-absolute hrefs; /api/v1/health -> 200 application/json. Log: /tmp/consensus-qa-20261021-live/live-probe.log.
IMPACT: any Go repo whose documented default listen port is written as host:port (not as a --port flag) and which has an extra loopback listener on a docs-mentioned/other port grades ui-probe INFO — i.e. the battery reports 'no HTML surface' while the repo's UI is fully served. This is the same surface QA-CONSENSUS-29 (closed) had to find BY HAND because the battery could not see it; the ui-probe arm therefore cannot serve as the regression guard for that class of fix.
FIX DIRECTION: resolve the repo's declared listen port from the product's own configuration (CONSENSUS_PORT/CONSENSUS_SERVER env, `--port` default, package.json dev/start script) and probe the DOCS list only as a supplement — never let a docs fallback displace the default; when the answering port serves no 2xx text/html on any documented path, treat it as 'not this repo's UI port' and continue scanning the remaining candidates instead of concluding there is no UI; keep the INFO wording for the genuinely no-surface case.

reasoning: DOGFOOD 2026-10-23, real-use drive of the /experimental/worktree family merged hours earlier (ROUTE-ADD-083/084/085/086, merges ae94992/db944ae/fcb4516, HEAD 1482437), scratch sqlite instance built from HEAD, /tmp/consensus-df-1023. The upstream contract (specs/openapi/upstream/openapi-1.18.33.json) declares for DELETE /experimental/worktree: query parameters directory+workspace (optional) AND request body WorktreeRemoveInput {directory: string, required}. Two independent deviations, both A/B-proven against the same binary: (A) BODY IGNORED. Server launched IN the repo (/tmp/consensus-df-1023/proj, port 18392): DELETE with the declared body only {"directory":"<linked worktree>"} -> 400 WorktreeRemoveFailedError "worktree.remove needs an explicit directory query parameter"; the identical request with ?directory=<linked worktree> and no body -> 200 true and the worktree really disappeared from disk and from `git worktree list`. The body is never read; only the query parameter is. The sibling reset handler is the opposite (DELETE-style body-less reset -> 400 InvalidRequestError kind=Body, body required), so the family is internally inconsistent: one op demands the declared body, the other silently ignores it. Provider: internal/shim/opencode/experimental_worktree_list_remove.go (handleExperimentalWorktreeRemove) reads only q.Get("directory") as the target. (B) DECLARED WORKSPACE SELECTORS IGNORED. Server launched OUTSIDE the repo (cwd /tmp/consensus-df-1023, port 18391 — the realistic case, e.g. a systemd unit with no WorkingDirectory): POST /experimental/worktree?directory=<repo> -> 200 and a real git worktree on disk (create DOES honour the declared selector, via worktreeCreateDeclaredDirectory, experimental_worktree_create.go:229-240); GET /experimental/worktree?directory=<repo> -> 200 listing it; then DELETE /experimental/worktree?directory=<that worktree> -> 400 WorktreeNotGitError "workspace /tmp/consensus-df-1023 is not a git repository: exit status 128", and reset -> 400 the same way. Cause: remove/reset take the workspace from apiV2LocationSelector (api_v2_lists.go:87-111), which reads only the bracketed location[directory]/location[workspace] selectors and otherwise falls back to requestWorkspaceDir -> header x-opencode-directory or the process CWD (server.go:3645-3665). SPEC-017 §3.10 pins the resolution order for the shim workspace as "x-opencode-directory, then the declared ?directory= selector, then ?workspace=, then the configured workdir" — the middle two are absent here, and worktree.remove/reset are the only handlers in the family that skip them. Workarounds proven live (both 200 true, worktree removed): add header x-opencode-directory=<repo>, or send ?location[directory]=<repo>. Net user impact: a client that creates a worktree (create honours ?directory=) can never remove it unless the server happened to be started inside the repo, so worktrees accumulate on disk; the failure message names an unrelated directory, which reads as a server fault rather than a selector problem. FIX DIRECTION: take the removal target from the declared body (WorktreeRemoveInput.directory) with the query parameter as an accepted alternative, and resolve the workspace in the SPEC-017 order for remove+reset so all four handlers agree. EVIDENCE: /tmp/consensus-df-1023/evidence (arm logs), full arms in docs/dogfood/2026-10-23-worktree-copy-surface.md, dogfood-log 2026-10-23 entry.

detail.text:
Filed by the dexdat-core foreman (tick dexdat-core-foreman-2026-11-02-15-08-46) as the owning-repo row for a gap that cannot be fixed inside dexdat/dexdat-core. Cross-reference: dexdat-core board row SC-SHIM-RESPONSE-TIMEOUT (P1, stays pending there until this ships) and dexdat-core docs/operators/sc-shim-response-timeout.md (root cause with file:line, rejected alternatives, verification recipe).

PROBLEM: internal/shim/opencode/server.go hard-codes `const defaultMessageResponseTimeout = 90 * time.Second` (line 150 at upstream main f95960d, verified 2026-11-02). The s.messageResponseTimeout field is initialized only at construction (server.go:164) and is settable only from _test.go files — CONSENSUS_TEST_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT is read nowhere outside tests (verified at f95960d). Any request whose processing outlives 90s gets 504 RESPONSE_TIMEOUT while the session is still healthy and later completes. Measured on the deployed dexdat-core stack (container dexdat-core-consensus-1, pinned rev 52bc6608): 7 x 'status=504 code=RESPONSE_TIMEOUT' in the same log window as 9 x 'planning: responding to user', planning wall max_turns=10 timeout=3m0s against deepseek-v4-pro at 7-48s per turn. POST /session/<id>/message returns 504 mid-planning on every planning session that runs long, which fails dexdat-core's tests/integration/test_consensus_e2e.py::TestSessionLifecycle::test_send_message_and_get_response at every HEAD.

REQUIRED CHANGE (this repo): make the message-response budget configurable through a supported production surface — e.g. a CONSENSUS_MESSAGE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT env var read in the shim server construction, or a WithMessageResponseTimeout option wired to the server config — keeping 90s as the default. A test-only override is not sufficient: consumers must set the budget above their planning wall (>= 3m) from deployment config.

NOT REQUIRED: no change to planning-wall semantics (max_turns/timeout stay as-is); no consumer-side changes here — dexdat-core will consume the surface in its own follow-up once this ships.
